number.why: The rejected HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.53–1.36) belongs to the primary composite. The proposed HR 1.77 (95% CI 0.81–3.87) correctly represents all-cause mortality for eplerenone versus placebo. The registry explicitly includes all randomized participants and specifies follow-up from randomization through the trial cutoff, including deaths after treatment discontinuation.

quotes.span: The primary endpoint was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes or hospitalization for HF. The primary endpoint occurred in 29.7% of patients in the eplerenone group vs. 32.7% in the placebo group [hazard ratio=0.85 (95% CI: 0.53-1.36)].
RESULT OUTCOME 2 [SECONDARY]: Number of Participants With With First Occurrence of All-Cause Mortality

Mortality during treatment, within 30 days of treatment discontinuation and after 30 days of discontinuation was reported. Hazard ratio of Eplerenone versus placebo for first occurrence of the event was obtained from a Cox proportional hazards model. | TIME FRAME: Randomization up to the date when the last enrolled participant had been followed up for 1 year (up to 1744 days) | POPULATION: Full analysis set included all randomized participants.

entry.why: The packet establishes adults with HFrEF receiving eplerenone versus placebo in a randomized, double-blind trial. The registry minimum age establishes adult eligibility.

quotes.span: We evaluated the efficacy and safety of eplerenone in patients with HFrEF in a multicenter, randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled outcome study (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01115855).
HFrEF patients with NYHA functional class II-IV and an EF ≤35% received eplerenone (n=111) or placebo (n=110) on top of standard therapy for at least 12 months.
ELIGIBILITY AGE/SEX: minimum age 55 Years | maximum age None | sex ALL

missed: No finding changes either verdict. The ruling understates the direct population and follow-up evidence: evidence/held/registry/NCT01115855.json explicitly states "Full analysis set included all randomized participants." and "TIME FRAME: Randomization up to the date when the last enrolled participant had been followed up for 1 year (up to 1744 days)". These establish the analysis population and mortality observation window more directly than matching denominators or dosing duration.
